label: Safe R

model.rationale: The district's R+23 lean, Jackson's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing him near 94% all point to a safe Republican hold; Nair's minimal fundraising offers no evidence of competitiveness.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or late outside spending surge against Jackson would be the only plausible path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
TX-13 is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Incumbent Ronny Jackson is running for reelection with a massive financial edge: over $5.4 million on hand after raising more than $4 million, plus modest outside support. Democrat Mark Nair has raised about $102,000 with just $14,000 remaining, and no outside groups are engaged on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Jackson roughly a 94% chance of winning. With the fundamentals, money, and markets all aligned, the seat is expected to remain safely in Republican hands in November.
